item.text:
Prayut Chan-o-cha in 2022 was Thailand’s prime minister and also defense minister, but his authority was unusually constrained by the 2017 constitution’s eight-year limit dispute, a Constitutional Court suspension, coalition arithmetic, parliament, and recurring protest pressure. I am not re-fetching the structured local facts you supplied; I am using them as the baseline and adding only the smallest set of narrative sources needed for ruler-specific context.

**What the local facts already establish**
- 2022 country-year conditions were weak on civil liberties, accountability, and governance, with low-level conflict and repression indicators already present in your local prior.
- The prior also already covers the major structured macro context for 2022, so I am not re-searching those dataset facts.
- For 7B and 8B in particular, the local prior already contains the WGI/V-Dem style governance evidence; I am not duplicating those values here.

**Retained Sources**
1. `Directory of Prime Ministers of Thailand` | Royal Thai Government / Secretariat of the Prime Minister | n.d. | [https://archives.thaigov.go.th/en/history/prime-minister](https://archives.thaigov.go.th/en/history/prime-minister)  
   Precise fact: Prayut is listed as the 29th prime minister. Period fit: office anchor for the whole 2022 period. Ruler attribution: official government roster. Limitations: it identifies the officeholder but does not explain legal constraints or policy performance. Contrary point: none on identity, but it is not evidence of effectiveness.

2. `The 14th session of the 25th House of Representatives meeting...` | Thai Parliament | page date 23 Aug 2022; session text refers to late July 2022 | [https://web.parliament.go.th/view/7/%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%A5%E0%B8%B0%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%B5%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7_EN/news%20%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%8A%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%98%E0%B9%8C/1136/EN-US](https://web.parliament.go.th/view/7/%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%A5%E0%B8%B0%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%B5%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7_EN/news%20%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%8A%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%98%E0%B9%8C/1136/EN-US)  
   Precise fact: the House rejected the no-confidence motion, 256 to 206, with 9 abstentions. Period fit: shows Prayut still had parliamentary support in 2022, but only narrowly. Ruler attribution: official vote record. Limitations: the page/date metadata are awkward, and it captures only the final vote. Contrary point: the motion itself shows durable opposition and coalition fragility.

3. `ศาลรัฐธรรมนูญรับคำร้อง "8 ปี ประยุทธ์" สั่งหยุดปฏิบัติหน้าที่` | Thai PBS News | 24 Aug 2022 | [https://www.thaipbs.or.th/news/content/318741](https://www.thaipbs.or.th/news/content/318741)  
   Precise fact: the Constitutional Court accepted the eight-year term petition and suspended Prayut from PM duties. Period fit: direct local-language coverage of the key 2022 legal shock. Ruler attribution: Thai-language independent reporting on the official court move. Limitations: a news report, not the judgment text. Contrary point: the article reflects the suspension moment only; it does not include the later ruling.

4. `Thai court clears way for PM Prayuth's return from suspension` | Reuters via Euronews | 1 Oct 2022 | [https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/01/thailand-politics](https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/01/thailand-politics)  
   Precise fact: the court ruled he had not exceeded the eight-year limit and could return after suspension. Period fit: closes the 2022 term-limit episode. Ruler attribution: Reuters reporting, republished by Euronews. Limitations: secondary reporting, not the full court text. Contrary point: the ruling was heavily contested by opponents who argued the junta period should count.

5. `รายงานผลการดำเนินงานของรัฐบาล พลเอก ประยุทธ์ จันทร์โอชา นายกรัฐมนตรี ปีที่ 3 (25 กรกฎาคม 2564 - 25 กรกฎาคม 2565)` | Secretariat of the Prime Minister | 28 Oct 2022 | [https://spm.thaigov.go.th/th/sub-org-15-265/content](https://spm.thaigov.go.th/th/sub-org-15-265/content)  
   Precise fact: the government published its year-3 performance report covering 25 Jul 2021 to 25 Jul 2022. Period fit: official favorable self-assessment for the 2022 period. Ruler attribution: direct government publication. Limitations: self-report; not independent validation. Contrary point: should be balanced against parliament, protests, and economic/rights reporting.

6. `IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Thailand` | IMF | 1 Sep 2022 | [https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/09/01/pr22299-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation-with-thailand](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/09/01/pr22299-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation-with-thailand)  
   Precise fact: the IMF said Thailand was recovering from the pandemic while inflation was rising and projected 2022 growth of 2.8 percent. Period fit: strong inherited-conditions source for the 2022 economy. Ruler attribution: macroeconomic context, not personal credit or blame. Limitations: country-level macro analysis, not ruler-specific. Contrary point: it supports resilience as well as constraint, so it should not be read as a simple success story.

7. `Thailand’s Economy Remains Resilient amid Global Headwinds` | World Bank | 14 Dec 2022 | [https://www.worldbank.org/th/news/press-release/2022/12/14/thailand-s-economy-remains-resilient-amid-global-headwinds](https://www.worldbank.org/th/news/press-release/2022/12/14/thailand-s-economy-remains-resilient-amid-global-headwinds)  
   Precise fact: the World Bank said Thailand’s economy had recovered to above pre-pandemic output in Q3 2022, with inflation elevated and poverty risks still present. Period fit: useful for 5B and 6B inherited-condition framing. Ruler attribution: country-level assessment during Prayut’s tenure, not proof of personal performance. Limitations: focuses on macro and fiscal conditions, not political causality. Contrary point: it highlights resilience and social-protection effects, which tempers a purely negative reading.

8. `Thai police use rubber bullets to disperse protest over APEC summit` | Reuters | 18 Nov 2022 | [https://theprint.in/world-news/thai-police-use-rubber-bullets-to-disperse-protest-over-apec-summit/1223029/](https://theprint.in/world-news/thai-police-use-rubber-bullets-to-disperse-protest-over-apec-summit/1223029/)  
   Precise fact: police fired rubber bullets to disperse APEC protesters; the protests were explicitly anti-Prayut. Period fit: major 2022 public-order and legitimacy event. Ruler attribution: Reuters event reporting. Limitations: short event report, limited broader context. Contrary point: police said protesters also assaulted officers.

9. `Thailand: Police Forcibly Disperse APEC Protesters` | Human Rights Watch | 22 Nov 2022 | [https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/11/22/thailand-police-forcibly-disperse-apec-protesters](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/11/22/thailand-police-forcibly-disperse-apec-protesters)  
   Precise fact: HRW said riot police used apparently excessive force, including beatings and rubber bullets, against APEC protesters. Period fit: strongest critical source on repression and policing in late 2022. Ruler attribution: directly frames Prayut’s government as responsible. Limitations: advocacy/reporting lens focused on one incident. Contrary point: it does not give the government’s full security rationale.

10. `Thailand: Rights Repressed` | Human Rights Watch | 12 Jan 2023 | [https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/01/12/thailand-rights-repressed](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/01/12/thailand-rights-repressed)  
    Precise fact: HRW said Prayut’s government pursued politically motivated prosecutions and violent dispersals throughout 2022. Period fit: broad 2022 repression summary. Ruler attribution: explicit attribution to the Prayut government. Limitations: published after the period, summarizing it retrospectively. Contrary point: should be triangulated with local reporting and the official court/parliament record.

**Compact event map**
- July 2022: Prayut survives a no-confidence vote, showing parliamentary backing but also brittle support.
- 24 Aug 2022: Constitutional Court suspends him over the eight-year term-limit challenge; Prawit steps in as acting PM while Prayut keeps the defense portfolio.
- 30 Sep 2022: Court clears him to return, ruling the term clock starts from the 2017 constitution.
- 18 Nov 2022: APEC protests in Bangkok end in clashes and a rubber-bullet response by police.
- Late 2022: the government presents an official performance narrative while external economic and rights sources describe recovery under strain, elevated inflation, and persistent repression.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- 1B: no strong ruler-specific web source set is needed here; your local prior already says there was no selected evidence, so I would not force a narrative claim.
- 2B: keep the local structured UCDP/SIPRI prior as the core; add Reuters protest/security reporting only if you need narrative context around security posture rather than conflict totals.
- 3B: use Thai PBS on the suspension, Reuters on APEC protests, and HRW on the crackdown; the local CIRIGHTS/PTS/UCDP/V-Dem prior remains the quantitative base.
- 4B: use the parliament vote record, Thai PBS suspension coverage, Reuters on the ruling, plus the local Freedom House/V-Dem/WGI priors already in hand.
- 5B: use IMF, World Bank, and the official PMO performance report; the local GDP/population priors remain the quantitative base.
- 6B: use IMF and World Bank plus the official PMO report; the local HDI/health priors already cover the baseline welfare numbers.
- 7B: do not re-fetch the local WGI/V-Dem corruption series; use the existing local prior plus the official PMO report for institutional self-framing.
- 8B: do not re-fetch the local WGI/V-Dem governance series; use the existing local prior plus the PMO report and the parliamentary/court record to separate capacity from legitimacy.
